items.title: Minority judge blocked, Dhana's tactics, government's pre-approval: Justice SK Kaul reveals inner workings of Collegium
items.summary: The questionable working of the Supreme Court Collegium - the body responsible for appointing judges to the higher judiciary - has been laid bare by one of its former members and retired Supreme Court Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul. In his memoirs titled Without Fear or Favour , the former judge most startlingly reveals that ex-Chief Justice of India (CJI) DY Chandrachud , as head of the Collegium, would seek the Central government's stance on potential appointments before consulting with the rest of the judges on the Collegium. The Collegium system was preserved by the Supreme Court in a bid to maintain judicial independence, free from executive influence. However, Justice Kaul seems to think that political considerations have long since crept, calling the method into question. In a scathing indictment of the system, he writes, "The collegium system worked well enough in the initial years, but over time, the judges have at times outdone the politicians. items.title: Theni jailbreak: 17 prisoners in TN escape after faking seizures, four of them caught
items.summary: The Tamil Nadu police have arrested four of the 17 remand prisoners who escaped from Thekkampatti sub-jail in Theni district on the night of Monday, October 26, after allegedly faking a medical emergency to draw prison staff into their cell and assaulting them. The first accused who was apprehended has been identified as Praveen Kumar. Three others — Silambarasan of Theni, and Raja Sikandar and Rajkumar, both from Madurai — were arrested during search operations in the early hours of October 27. Thirteen prisoners remain absconding, and police have launched a statewide search to trace them. According to preliminary investigations, all 17 prisoners were lodged in the same cell. At around 10.30 pm on October 26, some of them allegedly called the prison staff on duty, claiming that one of the inmates was suffering from epileptic seizures and needed medical assistance. When the prison staff opened the cell and entered to help, the inmates allegedly attacked them and fled the area at around 11 pm. items.title: Company directors not personally liable for unpaid legal fees: Bengaluru Court
items.summary: A Bengaluru civil court recently ruled in favour of law firm Krishnamurthy & Co. (K Law) in a suit seeking recovery of unpaid professional fees from Moerheim Roses and Trading India Private Limited, the Indian arm of a Dutch floriculture company. [K Law Vs Morheim Roses] In a judgment delivered on October 3, Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge Shirin Javeed Ansari directed the company to pay ₹2.75 lakh towards outstanding legal fees, along with interest at 9 percent per annum. However, the Court refused to hold the company's four directors personally liable for the dues. " The mere fact that a person is a director of a company does not, by itself, make such person personally liable for every contractual or commercial obligation of the company ," the Court observed. The dispute arose from legal services rendered by K Law in connection with a petition before the Karnataka High Court in 2017. According to the law firm, Moerheim Roses approached it through Delhi-based law firm Anand & Anand in January 2017. items.title: EAAS Model Service Agreement
items.summary: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy ( MNRE ) issued an office memorandum on 23 rd July 2026, introducing the Model Service Agreement for “ Electrolyser as a Service ” ( EAAS ). This model agreement outlines industry standards for risk allocation, performance guarantees, and division of responsibilities. It aims to improve the ease of doing business and streamline the contract negotiations between green hydrogen project developers and the consumers. Under the model agreement, the Service Provider designs, constructs, owns, operates, and maintains an electrolytic hydrogen plant ( H2 Plant ) on a Build, Own, and Operate basis at the site provided by the Service Recipient. The Service Provider retains exclusive ownership, title, and operational control over the H2 Plant, with no tenancy or hire-purchase or financing or deferred sale rights created in favour of the Service Recipient. The Service Provider must secure necessary insurance for the H2 Plant. The Service Provider is also permitted to encumber the H2 Plant for financing purposes. items.title: CoC can't withdraw approved insolvency resolution plan citing debtor's improved financial position: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday held that in corporate insolvency resolution proceedings, the Committee of Creditors (CoC) cannot withdraw an approved insolvency resolution plan merely by citing an improvement in the corporate debtor's financial position [ Bank of India & Ors. v. S.M. Kamal Pasha & Ors. ]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran held that a resolution plan becomes binding on both the CoC and the successful resolution applicant once it is approved by the creditors, even before its confirmation by the NCLT. The Court observed that the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC) does not permit either the CoC or the resolution applicant to withdraw from an approved resolution plan simply because subsequent developments have made the transaction financially less attractive. " We are of the opinion that the withdrawal of an application can only be till the CoC approves the plan and after it is placed before the Adjudicating Authority, there can be no withdrawal either of the application or the approved Resolution Plan," the October 26 judgment stated. items.title: Do not go to celebrities who charge for pollution awareness campaigns: Bombay High Court to State
items.summary: Public money cannot be spent to secure celebrity endorsements for civic awareness campaigns, the Bombay High Court observed on Monday during the hearing of petitions involving noise pollution in Mumbai [In re: Noise and Environmental Pollution]. A division bench of Justices GS Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale expressed sharp displeasure upon learning that film personalities were demanding commercial appearance fees to assist in anti-pollution drives. The issue arose after additional government pleader Jyoti Chavan informed the bench that authorities had approached celebrities to support the campaign, but they are asking for fees. Justice Kulkarni took strong exception to the disclosure: “Don't go to any celebrity who is going to charge you! If celebrities are not conscious about their own city, and they want to come only at fees, we are very sorry! We thought that there are celebrities who have a lot of social interest, sense of belonging to the city, and they would give it back,” the bench said. items.title: Bengaluru Police arrest three men for killing man in road rage attack
items.summary: Bengaluru’s Electronics City police have arrested three men for allegedly running over a 25-year-old man and dragging him beneath their car for around 100 to 150 metres, following a road altercation in Bengaluru. The victim, Ranjith Kumar Sahu, who was killed in the incident, was a native of Bihar working as a cook at a paying guest accommodation in BTM Layout. A fourth accused, identified as Shyam Kohar, remains absconding. The arrested men are Ajay Rabidas (26), Sajal Namasudra (19), and Bijoy Ray (27), all natives of Assam. The incident occurred around 1.50 am on October 21 near Pragathipura, within the limits of Electronics City police station. According to a complaint filed by Sahu’s friend, Nitish Kumar Mukhiya, a car approached their group at high speed as they were crossing the road after celebrating Dasara. When Mukhiya signalled the driver to slow down, the occupants allegedly took offence, made a U-turn and returned to confront the group. The confrontation escalated into an argument and an assault, following which Mukhiya called Sahu, who was at a nearby residence.
